historia.title: Iberian sanctuary & territory
historia.subtitle: 2,400 years ago, the Iberian aristocracy of Iltiraka claimed the wild Jandulilla valley

iberico_content.title: The heroic sanctuary of El Pajarillo (4th century BCE)
iberico_content.body:
Strategically situated atop a commanding hill in the Jandulilla River valley, the Iberian sanctuary of El Pajarillo is one of the most significant archaeological discoveries of Iberian protohistory (c. 350 BCE).
The commemorative monument was conceived as a grand stepped stage across three terraces of masonry and dressed stone blocks (sillares) for the apotheosis or heroization of an Oretanian prince or aristocrat. At its summit stood the celebrated sculptural ensemble staging the mythical combat between a young aristocrat and a wild beast: the imposing Wolf Head (Cabeza de Lobo), flanked by protective lions and winged griffins—a symbol of power, valor, and transcendence in Iberian culture.
iberico_content.facil: El Pajarillo is an archaeological site in Huelma. Over 2,300 years ago, the Iberians built a sacred place in memory of a hero. The stone sculptures were discovered in the fields and it is now protected by law.

iltiraka_content.title: The territory of Iltiraka: A valley to tame
iltiraka_content.body:
2,400 years ago, at the beginning of the 4th century BCE, the oppidum of Iltiraka —Úbeda la Vieja— set its sights on this valley. It decided to claim a wild territory: the valley of the Jandulilla River.
For the Iberian people, the Jandulilla valley was wild territory (silva): deep forest, the domain of wolves and mythical beings, a place where human power had not yet reached. They were territories they wanted to incorporate, and to do so required a hero capable of justifying it.
The oppidum of Iltiraka rolled out an ambitious occupation project: it established a settlement at Loma del Perro (between modern-day Úbeda and Jódar), controlled the routes ascending from the south, and built, at the headwaters of the river, a sanctuary in memory of its founding hero: El Pajarillo. Thus was born a territory transformed into the domain of a lineage (pagus).
iltiraka_content.facil: 2,400 years ago, the Iberian city of Iltiraka wanted to master this wild valley. To make it their own, they honored a hero and built a sacred sanctuary: El Pajarillo.

fontanar_content.title: A sacred landscape: the ritual path and El Fontanar
fontanar_content.body: A Sacred Landscape & El Fontanar: two sanctuaries articulated by a ceremonial ritual path...
fontanar_content.facil: The Iberians connected two sacred places along the river with a ceremonial path. Walking along it remembered the hero's journey and blessed the whole valley.

timeline.title: Chronological milestones and archaeological findings
timeline.subtitle: From the Iberian colonization of Iltiraka in the 4th century a.d. to systematic excavations and the declaration as a Cultural Heritage Site.

events.year: 6th–5th c. BCE · Early oppida & heroic sculptures
events.text: Fortified oppida emerge in the Upper Guadalquivir alongside dynastic sculptures like Cerrillo Blanco.

events.year: Early 4th c. BCE · Foundation of El Pajarillo sanctuary
events.text: Iltiraka colonizes the wild Jandulilla valley and erects the stepped sanctuary and Wolf monument.

events.year: Late 4th c. BCE · Crisis & ritual decommissioning
events.text: Crisis of clientelist aristocracies and ritual destruction/abandonment of El Pajarillo.
Discovery of the first Iberian lion sculpture during road construction between Solera and the N-324.
Discovery of the second lion and falcata warrior; emergency excavations by the University of Jaén.
Official declaration as Archaeological Zone BIC and opening of the accessible digital interpretation platform.
